subject: Headroom negotiation — prioritization request for CloudWave / Aurora AI
messages:
From: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@aurora.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@cloudwave.com
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity ask + timeline for CloudWave POC

Hi Naomi / Monica,

Thanks again for the demo last week. CloudWave (my customer) is close to committing to a 6-month POC that would require a dedicated pool to meet their low-latency throughput needs. Initial ask from procurement: 12 A100-equivalent GPUs reserved with 24/7 availability, start date target May 10th. They'd like to avoid multi-tenant hosting for data residency reasons.

High-level requirements from CloudWave:
- Average throughput: 700 tokens/sec sustained
- Peak bursts up to ~2.8M tokens/hour (daytime ops)
- KV cache warmup expected for real-time agents
- Strict request-level latency SLO: p95 < 220ms for short prompts

They understand this may require us to allocate from Dedicated capacity and are willing to sign a reserve if we can guarantee availability. Procurement also asked about fallback options if we can't fully dedicate the pool by May 10.

I've attached the spreadsheet they sent (cloudwave_capacity_request.xlsx). Can you confirm feasibility and what the gating decisions are? We need to present a delivery commitment to them by EOD Wednesday.

Thanks,
Alice
Solutions Architect, Aurora AI
(on behalf of CloudWave)

---

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@aurora.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask + timeline for CloudWave POC

Alice / Monica —

Thanks for the details and the spreadsheet. Monica — I added Rishi to loop infra/ops on sizing. Rishi, short summary: CloudWave is asking for a 12-A100 equivalent dedicated pool, start 2027-05-10, strict p95 latency SLO and high sustained throughput. They are open to a reserve contract.

Immediate questions for ops:
- Is there currently headroom in US Dedicated pools to carve 12 A100 equiv by May 10?
- If not, what are safe mitigation options (burst credits, staggered start, hybrid dedicated+hosted routing)?
- Any SLA exception required / risk to other reserved customers?

We need a recommendation by Wed EOD so Sales can finalize commitment language.

—Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask + timeline for CloudWave POC

+1 on the ask — we ran numbers this morning. Quick ops readout:

- Current US Dedicated footprint: 420 A100-equivalent slots across reserved pools.
- Committed/reserved: ~396 slots (includes Reserved contracts and active Dedicated customers).
- Standing headroom: ~24 slots (some are in warm standby for rolling upgrades).

That means we technically have the raw capacity to allocate 12 slots, BUT:
- Assigning those 12 would reduce headroom to ~12 slots, which removes our buffer for urgent oncall rebalances and short-notice enterprise bursts.
- Two upcoming near-term commitments (Nebula Systems onboarding, deal id NS-330) request 8 slots starting May 3 — those are currently soft-commits (sales verbal).

Risks if we prioritize CloudWave today:
1) If Nebula goes live May 3 we will be short ~8 slots and will need to preempt or migrate lower-tier customers, causing SLA churn risk.
2) Reduced headroom increases failure surface during rolling kernel upgrades and risk of transient p95 spikes.

Mitigation options:
A) Offer CloudWave a hybrid: 8 dedicated + 4 guaranteed burst credits on Hosted (satisfies residency question via VPC peering + egress controls). Delivery target May 10 feasible.
B) Push CloudWave start to May 24 to absorb Nebula if it converts — gives us time to free 12 slots via phasing down test pools.
C) Approve one-time preemption authority to reassign non-critical reserved capacity (requires leadership sign-off and customer credits).

Recommendation: present A (hybrid) as primary option and C as escalation fallback. Need leadership sign-off to approve preemption authority. Vivek — can you advise on customer-credit policy and whether we can short-term preempt older reserved pools?

Rishi
Head of Capacity Planning | Redwood Inference

---

On Mon, Apr 12, 2027 at 11:45 AM Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com> wrote:
> Naomi / Rishi / Monica —
>
> Thanks for the clear summary. Short answer: we do not want routine preemption. However, for strategic deals we can approve a one-off exception with a clear credit + SLA remediation package. Two points:
>
> 1) Finance needs a reconciliation: credits will be at least 25% of one month's reserved fee for an impacted customer for involuntary preemption. That cost must be charged to the deal (DW-4839) or covered by Sales/Rev Ops.
> 2) We need a policy record: moderation window (48 hrs notice if possible), rollback plan, and an audit trail (logs + customer notifications).
>
> If Sales is willing to take the credit + own the comms to the impacted customers, we can temporarily pull 12 slots and schedule the Nebula start to be sharded across Hosted fallback if they convert.
>
> I'll draft a short decision doc for sign-off (priority-allocation-decision.md).
>
> Vivek
> VP, Product Ops
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@cloudwave.com, Alice Zhang <alice.zhang@aurora.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Headroom negotiation — prioritization request for CloudWave / Aurora AI

Team —

Thanks for the fast turn. Sales position for customer: CloudWave is a strategic expansion opportunity in financial services vertical; they have a multi-year potential and will sign a 6-month paid reserve immediately if we can commit to the hybrid approach. Given Vivek's guidance, here's the decision we will present to CloudWave today:

1) Allocation: Carve 8 A100-equivalent GPUs into a Dedicated pool (start 2027-05-10).
2) Burst / headroom: Provide 4 A100-equivalent burst credits on Hosted with VPC peering and egress controls to satisfy residency during bursts.
3) Commercials: Sales will include a one-time operational credit to impacted customers in the amount Vivek outlined (finance-informed) and include the credit line in the DW-4839 contract.
4) Contingency: If Nebula converts before May 10 and we are short, Sales will immediately trigger the Hosted fallback and notify impacted customers. We'll log the incident and issue credits as required.

Action items:
- Monica: finalize the DW-4839 term sheet with the credit clause and get legal started on SLA exception language (attach sla-exception-form.pdf). Due EOD Wed.
- Rishi: carve the 8-slot Dedicated pool and configure the burst-credit policy for the CloudWave tenant. Confirm by EOD Wed.
- Vivek: share the short decision doc + approval signature block; Finance will confirm credit mechanics.

Naomi (Sales) will present this as the commitment to CloudWave at 18:00 PT today. If anyone sees a blocker to the above, reply ASAP.

Thanks all —
Naomi
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: cloudwave_capacity_request.xlsx; priority-allocation-decision.md; sla-exception-form.pdf
